title.narrative: Central Asia Regional Economic Cooperation Corridors 3 and 5 Enhancement Project

description.narrative: The impact of the project will be enhanced regional economic cooperation and inclusive economic growth in Tajikistan. The outcome will be improved regional network (CAREC corridors 3 and 5 and the subnetwork) connectivity. The project outputs will be (i) improved road conditions and enhanced road safety on CAREC corridors 3 and 5 (the Sayron-Karamyk road section, 88 km) and the subnetwork (the Vose-Khovaling road, 87 km) totaling 175 km; (ii) extended access to local communities through the improvement of rural feeder roads; and (iii) institutional strengthening of project management, contract supervision, and efficient road maintenance.

Output: Improved road conditions and enhanced road safety on CAREC corridors 3 and 5 and the subnetwork Indicator: 87 km road section from Vose to Khovaling rehabilitated and reconstructed with IRI of less than 3 m/km Achievement: 0.0 Progress/Status: The design-and-build contract for rehabilitation and reconstruction of Vose-Khovaling road for the total amount equivalent to $32.45 million was awarded to Sinohydro Corporation Ltd. on 28 September 2013 with completion date of 14 July 2016. The contractor commenced works on 14 January 2014.
On 15 June 2016, ADB approved extension of the contract implementation period by 6 months (until 14 January 2017) to accommodate additional works related to (i) unforeseen drainage works, (ii) unforeseen slope stability works and (iii) initially underestimated various quantities. In March 2017, ADB approved another 6-month extension of the contract (until 14 July 2017) to allow successful completion of the outstanding works, including additional safety features as required by the Road Police Department.
Rehabilitation works were completed; taking-over certificate was issued on 25 August 2017. Data Source: MOT project progress report and project completion report

Output: Improved road conditions and enhanced road safety on CAREC corridors 3 and 5 and the subnetwork Indicator: 88 km road section from Sayron to Karamik enhanced with IRI of less than 4 m/km Achievement: 0.0 Progress/Status: Contractor mobilization was slightly delayed owing in part to difficulties in securing visas for workers from People's Republic of China and adverse weather conditions in March and April 2015. Later the contractor made extra efforts and was able to bring the civil works progress largely back on track. During implementation, ADB approved four extensions of the contract implementation period, as detailed below:
(i) first extension of the contract implementation period by 6 months (until 18 October 2016) to accommodate additional works related to (a) prevention of rock slide, and (b) embankment protection works (approved in May 2016);
(ii) second extension until 31 December 2016 to allow completion of the remaining 2 km asphalt laying (approved in Nov 2016); and
(iii) third 8-month extension of the contract implementation period until 31 August 2017 to accommodate (a) additional works related to reconstruction and minor shift of road section at km 250 following flush water and mudflows in Surkhob river in June 2016, which washed out the ongoing works for construction of retaining walls on km 250 and resulted in disruption of road traffic between Tajikistan and Kyrgyzstan, as well as (b) changes in work quantities as per the final design against the preliminary one (approved in March 2017), and
(iv) fourth 3-month extension (until 30 November 2017) to allow completion of remedial works (a number of avalanches, earthquake and floods occurred during winter of 2017 caused a damage of the rehabilitated road, which had to be repaired / reconstructed; costs of reconstruction / repair will be covered by the insurance company).
Civil works were completed; taking-over certificate was issued on 8 December 2017. Data Source: MOT project progress report and project completion report

Output: Improved road conditions and enhanced road safety on CAREC corridors 3 and 5 and the subnetwork Indicator: 43 km road section Khovaling - Baljuvon - Kangurt road improved (through rehabilitation of the most deteriorated segments) Achievement: 42.5 Progress/Status: On 4 August 2017, ADB approved a minor change in Project to allow utilization of grant savings for rehabilitation of Khovaling - Baljuvon - Kangurt road. Output: Extended access to local communities Indicator: 30 km rural access roads improved Achievement: 0.0 Progress/Status: A total of $0.9 million was allocated to improve 30 km feeder roads along the Vose to Khovaling section. In May 2016, a selection committee comprising staffs from MOT and local road maintenance units, representatives at both village and district level, and PMC consultant identified the feeder roads, which are proposed for rehabilitation under the project in Vose and Khovaling districts. Totally, about 30 km of feeder roads were selected for rehabilitation, with the estimated rehabilitation cost of $1.8 million (approximately $0.9 million each contract). In October 2016, ADB approved increase in allocation for the rural road component from $0.9 million to $1.8 million.
Two civil work contracts for improvement of feeder roads along Vose to Khovaling road sections, respectively, were awarded in May 2017. Works started in June 2017. On 23 April 2018 ADB approved extension of both contracts (Vose and Khovaling) by 79 days (until 19 May 2018) to allow completion of works, as well as some minor changes in work scopes. Civil works have been completed. Data Source: MOT project progress report and project completion report Baseline value: 0 Baseline value: 0 Target year: 2017 Target value: 30 Actual value: 0.0

Output: Institutional strengthening Indicator: Road safety awareness training completed for local communities Achievement: Y Progress/Status: Road safety awareness program in Vose and Khovaling districts was completed. Road safety trainings were conducted by PMC's Road Safety Specialist covering 9 (100%) villages along Vose-Khovaling project road and about 5 villages along Sayron-Karamyk road. Another series of road safety awareness training for local communities in Vose and Khovaling was conducted by NGO in 2017. Following ADB's approval for rehabilitation of additional 43 km Khovaling - Baljuvon - Kangurt road section, Gender Consultant and qualified trainers in close cooperation with the local executive authorities of the Temurmalik and Baljuvon districts, conducted series of trainings covering 159 women on mini training on basics of road safety rules. Additionally, it is planned to conduct (a) informational campaign work on road safety issues for the schoolgirls (50%) and schoolboys (50%) of the schools located along the Kangurt-Baljuvon-Khovaling road, and (b) trainings on preparation of pair-lawyers (social lawyers) covering 50 % women and 50% men participants, by end of project. Data Source: MOT project progress report and project completion report Baseline value: N Baseline value: N Target year: 2017 Target value: Y Actual value: Y
